physical.title: Synthetic finite parallel Beam traverses true slab and returns from separated finite mirror

interpretation.requestedResult: Observe real PhyDemo Beam samples entering and leaving both faces of a finite slab around one reflected return from a strictly separated finite mirror.
assumptions: All indices, source coordinates and brightness, slab thickness 60 mm, exterior mirror separation 30 mm, finite mirror length 420 mm, passive source-side detector and sampling policy are synthetic teaching choices.
Two real vertical native PlaneGlass boundaries at x=0 and 60 delimit uniform refractive index 1.5 with exterior material 1 on BOTH sides; mirror at x=90 is separated from slab by 30 mm.
Both boundaries explicitly omit partial Fresnel reflections (partialReflection=false). Pinned native TIR remains; light paths are not prescribed.
The backing mirror is not in direct contact with slab; this is NOT a full simulation of original JEE J08, whose mirror rests on the plate.
unknowns: No direct touching/co-planar mirror+glass qualification is supported by this new native profile.
No 3D observer, image reconstruction, calibrated irradiance, source-identified ray ancestry or original textbook-answer completeness is inferred.
